newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to delay LNG purchase from Oman.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to delay LNG purchase from Oman.

text.p: Thailand delayed its earlier plan to buy 1.7-2.2 million tonnes a year of liquefied natural gas from Oman due to its reservation about prices quoted, a senior industry ministry official said on Monday.
The Thai and Oman governments signed a memorandum of understanding in August 1996 to buy the LNG from Oman for 25 years, starting from 2003, the official said.
Under the MOU, which was signed by the previous government, both parties were supposed to officially sign a purchase contract in March.

But the Thai government had recently notified the Oman government of its decision to delay the contract signing after Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi expressed reservations about the deal. He had said he would like to study LNG projects in other countries before making a decision, the official said.
"The minister will go to Japan by the end of this month to examine the country's LNG operations before making a decision. The delay should not be interpreted as cancellation," the official said.
Other ministry sources told Reuters that with Indonesia's mega natural gas project Natuna now in the picture, buying LNG from Oman has become less attractive.
"Studies show that LNG prices from Oman are higher than natural gas from around this area. The government will have to come up with a very good reason to buy from Oman," one of the sources said.
